bull_bear.body: Debt-free balance sheet with INR68cr net cash (consol) and ~INR1,000cr liquid investments at parent; Capex self-funded by subsidiary cash flows; Parent liquidity acts as safety net; No dividend specifics given but strong cash generation supports potential payouts.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 100% reliance on imported aerospace-grade raw materials (supply chain/geopolitical risk); Execution risk on Andhra facility timeline (late FY28); Global OEM certification delays; Potential lag in passing through raw material cost inflation; Concentration in engine components (75%) though diversified across OEMs.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and execution-focused; Emphasizes 'derisking' customer base and moving up value chain; Transparent about one-offs (land gain, interest income shift); Modular growth approach to capex (machinery ordered quarterly based on ramp-up) rather than big-bang; Long-term optimism on India's role in global aerospace supply chain.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The flat consolidated EBITDA is an accounting artifact of the Realty demerger (loss of interest income on INR600cr cash transfer), masking a actual ~20% operational EBITDA growth; The company is transitioning from a job-shop model to a 'co-design' partner (build-to-spec), which fundamentally changes valuation multiples; Machinery procurement is continuous and modular (every quarter) to match SKU ramp-up, avoiding large single-point capex risks.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net cash surplus of ₹68 Cr (FY26), with a dedicated slide headed "Raymond Limited to Remain Net Cash Surplus".
- "Zero Non-Core asset distraction. Capital management bandwidth and cash flows are now 100% dedicated to precision engineering compounding."
- The demerged Raymond Lifestyle is described as having an "Independent Capital Structure"; the deck states no dividend, buyback or leverage policy for Raymond Limited.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Market leadership in Ring Gears and Steel Files segments in India
- Long-standing relationships (2+ decades) with leading global aerospace OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers, supported by high entry barriers and stringent qualification requirements
- Positioned as a Global 'Tier 1.5' aerospace partner offering one-stop-shop capabilities across machining, assembly and specialised processes, combined with competitive 'best cost country' manufacturing
- Diversified engineering portfolio across Precision Technology, Auto Components, Tools & Hardware and Aerospace & Defence, reducing dependence on any single industry segment
- Export-led model with presence across 65+ export countries and 18+ global customer locations
- Aerospace order book exceeding INR 2,350 crore over the next five years, providing revenue visibility
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Exposure to global cyclical industries — The Company's aerospace and auto-component businesses remain sensitive to global demand cycles, economic slowdowns and geopolitical uncertainties, which may impact order inflows and profitability.
- High capital expenditure requirements — Raymond is undertaking significant investments towards capacity expansion (Andhra Pradesh and Gudipalli facilities) and advanced manufacturing facilities, which may temporarily exert pressure on operations.
- Margin pressure from input cost volatility — Fluctuations in prices of aerospace-grade metals and raw materials may affect operating margins, particularly during periods of supply chain disruption and inflationary pressure.
- Geopolitical and supply chain risks — Ongoing geopolitical conflicts, trade disruptions and logistics bottlenecks may impact raw material availability, exports and operational efficiency across global markets.
- Intensifying global competition — The engineering and aerospace sectors remain highly competitive, with global players continuously investing in technology, innovation and cost efficiencies.
- Regulatory and compliance challenges in Aerospace & Defence — Aerospace and defence businesses are subject to stringent certifications, quality standards and regulatory approvals, which may lead to operational or project execution risks if not managed effectively.
- Long product qualification and approval cycles — The aerospace business involves long product qualification and approval cycles, while evolving customer requirements in EVs, aerospace and precision engineering necessitate continuous investment in technology, quality systems and manufacturing capabilities.
- Demand volatility in key export markets — The Company remains exposed to global trade uncertainties and demand volatility across key export markets, particularly Europe, and the automotive and aerospace sectors, compounded by supply chain disruptions and raw-material price fluctuations affecting delivery schedules and costs.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Corporate restructuring is described as complete: Raymond Lifestyle (listed Sep 05, 2024) and Raymond Realty (listed Jul 01, 2025) are demerged and listed, leaving Raymond Limited as a pure-play engineering company with "Zero Non-Core asset distraction".
- Aerospace arm is positioned as "the leading exporter of highly critical Aero engine components" from India and a "Preferred Supplier To top 3 Global Aircraft Engine Manufacturers holding 88% market share", with 25+ global aero components clients and 2 decades of relationships with top OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers.
- The stated moat is qualification lock-in: programmes run [RFQ Bidding] to [Prototype R&D Sample] to [First Article Inspection (FAIR)] to [10-Year Mass Production], and "Once FAIR qualification is achieved, OEM platform switching costs are prohibitive, ensuring zero customer churn".
- Precision Technology & Auto Components is positioned on category leadership, claiming "#1 in India" for Steel Files and for Ring Gears, and "one of India's leading suppliers of high-end precision components" with 7 decades as a Tier-1 supplier and 100+ large customers globally.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demerger] Raymond Lifestyle listed Sep 05, 2024 carrying Branded Textiles & Apparel and Global Garmenting B2B; Raymond Realty listed Jul 01, 2025 carrying Thane land bank development and an MMR asset-light JDA model, described as a "Top-5 Developer in MMR".
- [Legal entities] Aerospace & Defence is operated through JK Maini Global Aerospace Ltd. (the A&D division of erstwhile Maini Precision) and Precision Technology & Auto Components through JK Maini Precision Technology Ltd. (T&H division, RPAL and the Auto division of erstwhile Maini Precision).
- [Defence traction] Mass production of precision components began for a leading defence OEM; formal audit approvals were achieved from a key Indian defence and aerospace OEM; and a maiden build-to-spec order was received from a leading defence aerospace OEM, alongside development of specialised onboard storage systems.
- [Localization programme] On a flagship aircraft localization program the company secured "135 total part awards—with 100 parts actively in serial production and the remaining 35 parts advancing through final First Article Inspection (FAI)".
- [Governance] The deck flags a "Comprehensive upgrade of leadership, governance, and organizational capabilities", with senior management of 30+ years' industry expertise cited for both segments.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Following the demerger of the Lifestyle business (to Raymond Lifestyle Limited) and the Real Estate business (to Raymond Realty Limited), Raymond Limited now holds its Engineering business through majority-owned subsidiaries JK Maini Precision Technology Limited (Precision Technology & Auto Components, Tools & Hardware) and JK Maini Global Aerospace Limited (Aerospace & Defence), and its Denim business through a 50% joint venture, Raymond UCO Denim Private Limited. The group supplies precision-engineered automotive, industrial and aero-engine components to domestic and global OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers; at the standalone Raymond Limited level, the Company's own disclosed turnover comes from Aviation and Investment activities.

- **Tools & Hardware:** Files, Power tools, Cutting tools, Power tool accessories, Hand tools
- **Aerospace & Defence:** Aero-engine components, Structural parts, System assemblies, Casting programmes, Vanes
- **Raymond UCO Denim (Joint Venture):** Denim fabrics, Denim garments

business.title: Group structure (profile)

business.body:
- Market leadership in Ring Gears and Steel Files segments in India
- Long-standing relationships (2+ decades) with leading global aerospace OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers, supported by high entry barriers and stringent qualification requirements
- Positioned as a Global 'Tier 1.5' aerospace partner offering one-stop-shop capabilities across machining, assembly and specialised processes, combined with competitive 'best cost country' manufacturing
- Diversified engineering portfolio across Precision Technology, Auto Components, Tools & Hardware and Aerospace & Defence, reducing dependence on any single industry segment
- Export-led model with presence across 65+ export countries and 18+ global customer locations

business.title: Competitive strengths

latest_quarter.body: Aerospace margins stable at 22-25% despite 100% imported raw materials (Titanium, Inconel); Auto margins expanded 240bps FYoY due to operational synergies, SAP integration, and product mix, partially aided by INR13cr land gain; Near-term pressure expected from raw material inflation but pass-through mechanisms active; Localization of raw materials (6-8 month timeline) identified as key future margin lever.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue CAGR ~25% for Aerospace over next 2 years; Auto margins sustainable at ~13-14% excluding one-offs; Order inflow steady with 250-350 new SKUs/year; Capex INR930cr over 5 years (INR500cr Aero, INR430cr Auto); New Andhra facility commissioning late CY2027 (Q4 FY28) contributing meaningful revenue from FY29.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: INR2,350cr (Aerospace specific); >10-year visibility on global aircraft backlog; 75% of book tied to engine programs across multiple OEMs (derisked from single platform); RFQ pipeline converting to multi-year contracts.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Migration to 'build-to-spec' (design ownership) vs traditional 'build-to-print'; Expansion into aerostructures, landing gear, and hydraulics (currently 25% of mix); Gas turbine segment exploration; 300-350 new components added annually; Andhra greenfield facility enabling 2x capacity scale.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Multi-horizon planning framework — a 10-year vision, a 5-year strategic roadmap, and a detailed Annual Operating Plan (AOP) driving execution, reviewed through defined KPIs and monthly/quarterly reviews.
- Growth primarily driven through organic initiatives, underpinned by continuous innovation.
- Balanced, portfolio-led approach to the EV transition rather than a binary shift — building hybrid-component exposure while its core four-wheeler and commercial-vehicle exposure transitions gradually.
- Customer-led demand visibility — deepen participation across existing and new customer programmes, RFQ pipelines and confirmed order visibility, and increase share of business with existing OEMs and Tier-1 partners.
- Shift towards higher value-added, precision-engineered components and deeper co-design/assembly integration with customer platforms to enhance margin profile.
- Geographic diversification and global exposure to reduce concentration risk and participate in global supply chains.
- Driving Industry 4.0 / digitalisation integration across operations, including real-time monitoring of machine performance (OEE).
- Positioned as a Global 'Tier 1.5' aerospace partner, deepening programme participation (e.g. LEAP engine programme, casting programmes, new product categories such as vanes) and expanding into new geographies (UK, Belgium, Sweden).
- Deepening share of wallet with top-10 OEM customers via Just-in-Time (JIT) warehousing established in the US and Europe.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Raymond Limited, through its subsidiaries JK Maini Precision Technology Limited (JKMPTL) and JK Maini Global Aerospace Limited (JKMGAL), is progressing a new aerospace manufacturing facility in Andhra Pradesh — a ₹510 crore investment designed to produce high-precision aero-engine parts for leading global OEMs — alongside a new ₹430 crore automotive component facility at Gudipalli positioned within India's evolving EV supply chain, together a combined ~₹1,000 crore capital allocation committed to support multi-year backlogs. During FY2026 the Aerospace & Defence segment was described as 'progressing steadily' on the Andhra Pradesh expansion project with planned long-term capacity addition. JKMPTL was formed by unifying the erstwhile Tools & Hardware business, Ring Plus Aqua Limited and the auto business of Maini Precision Products Limited into a single integrated platform and now operates 15 integrated manufacturing facilities; separately, the Company's Precision Technology & Auto Components / Tools & Hardware operations comprise 16 manufacturing facilities across 4 locations in India (Nashik, Vapi, Chiplun, Bengaluru), supported by 1,800+ machines and 11 global 3PL warehouses.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India remained one of the fastest-growing major economies in FY2025-26, supported by strong domestic demand, infrastructure spending and improving manufacturing activity; real GDP growth estimated at 7.7% (FY2026-27 projected at 6.6%).
- Indian precision engineering market is expected to grow from USD 536 million (2025) to USD 996 million by 2034, driven by automation, smart manufacturing and localisation initiatives.
- Auto components demand remains strong across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles and tractors, supported by infrastructure spend, rural cash flows and increasing localisation/EV-hybrid adoption; commercial vehicle EV penetration nearly doubled to 1.83% and passenger vehicle EV share rose to 4.25% in FY26.
- India aerospace & defence market is expected to reach nearly USD 54.4 billion by 2033 (CAGR ~8.1%), driven by defence modernisation, indigenisation and rising aircraft demand.
- EV adoption is segment-specific, skewed towards two-wheelers, while the Group's core four-wheeler/commercial-vehicle exposure is expected to transition more gradually towards hybrid powertrains; ~10% of revenues are already linked to hybrid components with a roadmap for further scaling, and a further ~10% of revenues come from non-automotive segments (hydraulics, industrial, locomotive, marine, power tools).
- In flexplates, the domestic market is estimated at ~0.6-0.65 million units annually with realisations of ~₹565-570 per unit; in ring gears, annual production exceeds 10 million units, with demand supported by low BEV penetration and continued reliance on ring gears even in mild-hybrid vehicles.
- Aerospace segment revenue is highly export-oriented (~79% from exports); LEAP engine programme contributed ~₹110 crore (Apr 2025-Feb 2026), legacy CFM56 programme ~₹1.5 crore and other programmes ~₹20 crore, with the portfolio mix shifting towards more complex LEAP components.
- Commercial aviation represents ~86% of the aerospace segment mix, complemented by defence and other segments, giving a balanced and resilient portfolio.
- Aerospace & Defence order book exceeding INR 2,350 crore over the next five years.
- LEAP engine programme contribution of ~₹110 crore (Apr 2025-Feb 2026), with legacy CFM56 (~₹1.5 crore) and other programmes (~₹20 crore) continuing to contribute, and the portfolio mix shifting toward more complex LEAP components.
- Secured nominations for multiple components and assemblies from a European advanced drivetrain technology company.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Raymond's engineering arm delivered resilient double-digit growth in Aerospace (26% FY26) and margin expansion in Auto (13.4% vs 11%), driven by global OEM diversification and operational synergies, while guiding for a transformative INR930cr capex to double capacity via a new Andhra facility by late FY28. The shift from 'build-to-print' to 'build-to-spec' and a record order book provide multi-year visibility despite near-term raw material import dependencies.

meta.thesis: Raymond's engineering arm delivered resilient double-digit growth in Aerospace (26% FY26) and margin expansion in Auto (13.4% vs 11%), driven by global OEM diversification and operational synergies, while guiding for a transformative INR930cr capex to double capacity via a new Andhra facility by late FY28. The shift from 'build-to-print' to 'build-to-spec' and a record order book provide multi-year visibility despite near-term raw material import dependencies.
